sources.claim: Commercial bank interest rate on credit card plans, accounts assessed interest: 22.36% (2026 Q3, preliminary); all accounts 21.19%. Fed G.19 released Nov 6, 2026, fetched Nov 18, 2026.
FOMC maintained the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on Oct 28, 2026 (vote 10-2).
Charge-off rate on credit card loans, all commercial banks: 3.82% (Q2 2026, seasonally adjusted), FRED, fetched Nov 18, 2026.
Python: 22.36 - 4.00 = 18.36 points gap; 18.36 - 3.82 = 14.54 points; 22.36 / 4.00 = 5.59x. The split is a rough illustration, not an accounting breakdown.

post.instagram_caption:
Why is your credit card 22% when the Fed's rate is 4%?

The Fed's own data: card accounts paying interest averaged 22.36% in Q3 2026. The Fed's key rate range tops out at 4% (held on Oct 28, 2026). That's an 18-point gap. Roughly 3.8 points of it is risk: banks wrote off 3.82% of card loans (Q2 2026), because card debt has no house or car behind it. The other 14.5 points or so covers running costs, rewards and the bank's margin. Rough illustration, not an accounting breakdown.
